body.cap: Exhibition products showcased by FirstHabit at CES 2026 Unveiled on January 4. The featured product, “CHALK,” received Innovation Awards in two categories at this year’s CES. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: FirstHabit (CEO Dakyeom Jang) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

FirstHabit is an edtech startup that has developed AI models and learning platforms specialized for education. Since its founding in 2022 under its former name “Seomjae,” the company has accumulated extensive lecture, question, and solution data from real educational settings and has continued research into AI architectures and interfaces tailored to educational purposes.

The outcome of this research and the company’s core competency lies in its visual large language model technology. Leveraging this capability through “CHALK AI,” FirstHabit joined the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) Alliance in 2024 and demonstrated its technological reliability and educational effectiveness by producing CES Innovation Award winners for two consecutive years, including this year.

CHALK AI is an education-dedicated AI model branded as “The First Visual LLM Built for Education.” Unlike conventional LLMs that provide only text-based answers, it visually guides concept formation and step-by-step problem-solving by combining formulas, diagrams, and graphs. According to the company, this approach allows learners to focus on conceptual understanding and the flow of reasoning rather than simply arriving at correct answers.

To ensure that visual LLMs operate effectively in educational environments, FirstHabit designed its explanation methods and criteria for selecting visual materials based on foundational research grounded in a cognitive model. This model analyzes learner responses to assess the suitability of matching visual materials with explanatory sequences and enables the implementation of interfaces aligned with educational objectives.

“CHALK,” which translates these technologies into an actual learning experience, is a platform designed to accelerate conceptual understanding through visual LLMs. It attracted strong interest from North American media and industry stakeholders who visited the CES 2026 Unveiled venue.

body.cap: The FirstHabit booth at CES 2026 Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: CHALK also received favorable responses for integrating interactive lectures, real-time problem-solving support, learning diagnostics, and curriculum management into a UI centered on the learning flow. In addition, it gained recognition for its clear differentiation, dynamically adjusting explanation styles and visual materials based on comprehension levels, particularly in math and science learning.

A FirstHabit representative said, “Through this event, we were able to confirm positive feedback from North American audiences regarding CHALK AI’s visual LLM-based learning approach.” The representative added, “Especially in math and science demos, we saw responses indicating that visual explanations and interactive learning flows enhance actual learning outcomes, which has strengthened our confidence in the U.S.-focused market strategy we are preparing.”

The representative continued, “At the upcoming CES 2026 main exhibition, we plan to gather further feedback and reflect it in our technology development while accelerating the process of establishing a U.S. subsidiary and expanding pilot programs.” The representative added, “To that end, we will actively pursue collaboration with educational institutions, content producers, and edtech companies capable of integrating diverse local content into the CHALK platform.”

Meanwhile, the company will also participate in the leading CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, CES Unveiled.

‘CES Unveiled’ is a key official event held before the CES opening, bringing together Innovation Award winners and companies showcasing cutting-edge products. The event brings together global media, company executives, government officials, and significant technology industry stakeholders in one place.
